name: Transformer-based Reconstruction
text:
# Transformer-based Reconstruction

Also called: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting, Single-view/Sparse-view 3DGS Reconstruction

## Overview
Transformer-based Reconstruction refers to a family of feed-forward neural network methods that directly predict [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) parameters from 2D image inputs, bypassing the [iterative optimization loops](#5325-training-pipeline.md) typical of traditional 3DGS [S1, unofficial]. It solves the latency bottleneck of scene reconstruction by replacing gradient-based optimization with a single inference pass [S1, unofficial]. It differs from its siblings by utilizing [transformer architectures](#8998-transformer-based-architectures.md) to map image features directly to Gaussian attributes (mean, covariance, color, opacity) rather than relying on volume rendering quadrature or iterative density editing [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the following mechanism:
1.  **Input Encoding:** 2D images are encoded into feature tokens using a vision backbone (e.g., ViT) [S1, unofficial]. Camera parameters (intrinsics/extrinsics) are encoded into token embeddings if multi-view inputs are used [S1, unofficial].
2.  **Transformer Processing:** A transformer encoder/decoder processes the concatenated sequence of image and camera tokens to model spatial and geometric relationships [S1, unofficial].
3.  **Direct Parameter Prediction:** The network outputs a set of 3D Gaussian parameters ($\mu, \Sigma, c, \alpha$) directly, without intermediate volume rendering or iterative refinement [S1, unofficial].
4.  **Training Objective:** Models are supervised using photometric losses (e.g., LPIPS, SSIM) between rendered outputs and ground truth images during training [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Flash3D](1481-flash3d.md)
A feed-forward network for monocular 3DGS reconstruction. It estimates depth from a single image and predicts Gaussian parameters. Choose this for single-view inputs where depth estimation is feasible.

### [GS-LRM](1483-gs-lrm.md)
A feed-forward transformer for sparse-view (2-4 images) 3DGS reconstruction. It tokenizes image and camera data to predict Gaussians. Choose this for sparse multi-view scenarios requiring explicit pose conditioning.

### [Large Reconstruction Model (LRM)](5959-large-reconstruction-model-lrm.md)
A feed-forward model for single-image to 3D reconstruction. It predicts scene parameters in one step. Choose this for general single-view 3D generation tasks, potentially outputting [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) fields or meshes depending on the variant.

## Background
The method originates from the need to accelerate 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) reconstruction, which traditionally requires per-scene optimization [S1, unofficial]. Feed-forward approaches were developed to enable real-time reconstruction from single or sparse views by leveraging transformer architectures to generalize from large datasets of image-3D pairs [S1, unofficial].
